title: The schematic closure inside a Noetherian compactification
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$ be a compactification [def-nagata-compactification] with
$\overline X$ Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact), let $i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the
scheme-theoretic image of $j$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], and put $V=\overline X\setminus Z$ with open
immersion $j_V:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$. Then:

1. $j$ factors as $j=i\circ j_Z$ with $j_Z:X\hookrightarrow Z$ a
   quasi-compact open immersion, and $j_Z$ is scheme-theoretically dense;
1. $\overline X$ and $Z$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $V$ is a
   quasi-compact open of $\overline X$ whose closed complement is $Z$;
1. $j(X)\cap V=\varnothing$, so $X\times_{\overline X}V=\varnothing$ and
   $X\times_{\overline X}Z=X$ (via $j_Z$);
1. $p\circ i:Z\to S$ is proper.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-compactification], $j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper. Use only these clauses of the compactification definition, as in the current blueprint. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open $W$ of the Noetherian scheme $\overline X$ is quasi-compact. In particular $\overline X$ itself is quasi-compact. The intersection of any two affine opens is open, hence quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](2), applied to the affine open cover, makes $\overline X$ quasi-separated. For an affine open $A\subseteq\overline X$, $j^{-1}(A)$ is, via the open-subscheme identification of [def-weil-open-immersion], the open $j(X)\cap A$ of $\overline X$, and is therefore quasi-compact. For $j_V$, its inverse image $j_V^{-1}(A)$ identifies with $V\cap A$, which is open in $\overline X$ and hence quasi-compact by the same cited Noetherian-open statement. Thus $j$ and $j_V$ are quasi-compact morphisms by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; taking $W=V$ also proves that $V$ is quasi-compact as a space.

proof.text: An open immersion is an immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]: take the identity closed immersion of $X$ (the affine quotient by the zero ideal), followed by $j$. Step 1 supplies the quasi-compactness required by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image]. Applying that statement to $j$ gives a quasi-compact open immersion $j_Z:X\to Z$ with scheme-theoretically dense image. The canonical image factorization equality of [def-nagata-scheme-image-factor] gives $i\circ j_Z=j$. This proves (1). No reducedness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion), quasi-compact case; blueprint proof, second paragraph

proof.text: By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i$ identifies the underlying space of $Z$ with a closed subset $F$ of $\overline X$. Every open $W$ of $Z$ has the form $F\cap O$ for an open $O$ of $\overline X$. The open $O$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and $F\cap O$ is closed in $O$. To see its quasi-compactness directly, extend a relative open cover of $F\cap O$ to open subsets of $O$ and add $O\setminus F$; a finite subcover of $O$ restricts to a finite subcover of $F\cap O$. Taking $W=Z$ proves quasi-compactness of $Z$. Taking $W$ to be the intersection of any two affine opens of $Z$ and applying [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](2) proves that $Z$ is quasi-separated. Finally $V=\overline X\setminus F$ is open and its complement is precisely the underlying closed subset of the given closed subscheme $Z$. Together with step 1 this proves (2); the argument retains the given scheme structure on $Z$.

source.place: First paragraph (qcqs assertions), with the elementary closed-subspace finite-cover argument expanded instead of asserting that closed subschemes are Noetherian

proof.text: By the equality $j=i\circ j_Z$ from step 2, $j(X)$ is contained in $F=i(Z)$ and is disjoint from $V=\overline X\setminus F$. If the scheme $P=X\times_{\overline X}V$ of [def-pc-fibre-product] had a point, its two projections would send that point to points of $X$ and $V$ with the same image in $\overline X$, contradicting this disjointness. Hence $P$ has no points and is the empty scheme (the sheaf on the empty space is unique).

source.place: Third paragraph, first two sentences: disjointness and the empty fibre product

proof.text: A closed immersion $i$ is a monomorphism by the affine quotient description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Indeed, let $u,v:T\to Z$ satisfy $i\circ u=i\circ v$. For each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\overline X$, the common inverse image of $U$ in $T$ is open; cover it by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Both restricted maps land in $i^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and the induced ring maps $A/I\to B$ agree because their composites with the surjection $A\to A/I$ agree. Thus $u$ and $v$ agree on an open cover of $T$, so $u=v$. Put $Q=X\times_{\overline X}Z$ with projections $a:Q\to X$ and $b:Q\to Z$. By [def-pc-fibre-product] the pair $(\mathrm{id}_X,j_Z)$ defines $s:X\to Q$, and $a\circ s=\mathrm{id}_X$. The pullback equality and step 2 give $i\circ b=j\circ a=i\circ j_Z\circ a$, so monicity gives $b=j_Z\circ a$. The two projections of $s\circ a$ are now $a$ and $b$, so pullback uniqueness gives $s\circ a=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism with inverse $s$, and its projection to $Z$ is $j_Z$. This is the canonical identification $X\times_{\overline X}Z\simeq X$ in (3).

source.place: Third paragraph, last two sentences: explicit inverse to the base-change projection

proof.text: The compactification hypothesis gives properness of $p$ by [def-nagata-compactification], and $i$ is the given closed immersion. Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] with $f=p$ to conclude that $p\circ i:Z\to S$ is proper, proving (4).
